The pipeline on the new shoes, in pictures

A visual companion to the report "Where RACs fall on new shoes": how each of the 631 new prints was calibrated, outlined, cleaned and standardized, and the pictures behind the goodness of fit. Each figure names the file it comes from.

9 November 2026  |  Branch feature/new-shoes-finish

1. Putting the RACs on the image

The RAC coordinates come from a separate file, so they must be placed on each print's image with the right scale and orientation. The scale and orientation were chosen from the data: the mapping that puts the most RACs on a pixel where the sole touches the paper.

2. The outline of every shoe (the snake)

An active contour, the "snake", finds the outline of each print. It starts from an ellipse, shrinks onto the print, and is then refined. The same seven shoes (nos. 1–7) are shown at each step; the full sheets for all 631 shoes are in docs/qa/sheets_new/.

Stickers and frame lines

Some scans carry stickers, labels or frame lines next to the print. The same four steps for shoes 36–42 show how they are removed: shoe 36 loses 333 pixels of sticker debris (red in the last row) and shoe 37 loses 39.

Shoes that needed a fallback

For 23 shoes the standard snake missed part of the print (a narrow heel or toe, a faint region). They were rerun with a larger closing radius, and one shoe (170) with its own starting ellipse. Every case was checked by eye before and after.

3. The prototype

The prototype is the shape that the prints share when they are laid on top of each other. The new collection's prototype is used to clean its images; the model coordinates of both collections use the original prototype, so that the two live on one shoe.
